title: Legislate the Date to End Live Sheep Export Bill 2024
short_title: Legislate the Date to End Live Sheep Export Bill 2024

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend the Export Control Act 2020 to set 1 May 2026 as the legislated end date for the phase-out of live sheep exports by sea.
It would insert a new section 23A making the export of livestock sheep by sea from Australian territory absolutely prohibited on and after that date.
The whole Act would commence the day after it receives Royal Assent, and the statement of compatibility says the bill does not engage any applicable rights or freedoms.
changes: Section 12 would gain a definition of sheep that includes the young of the animal, so the prohibition would apply to livestock sheep of any age.
New section 23A would sit in the subdivision of the Act that deals with permanently prohibited goods.
Breaches of the new prohibition would be dealt with under the existing offence and civil penalty provisions in Division 4 of Part 1 of Chapter 2 of the Act.
summary.affected: Exporters of livestock sheep by sea from Australian territory are affected.
